title: Coordinated release ramp and stakeholder burnup for runtime/console/api
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Coordinate a single, stakeholder-visible release ramp across runtime, console and API surfaces that produces a daily burnup for owners, a capacity forecast for SRE, and a launch window reservation for sales/CS. Deliverables: a shared calendar (calendar-as-code), burnup dashboard, a compact runbook with rollback criteria and a checklist for feature gates. Success metrics: zero cross-surface deployment collisions during ramp window, <5% variance between forecast and actual capacity used, and stakeholder readiness >90% before canary.
acceptance_criteria: Shared calendar published and hooked to guardrail automation
Burnup dashboard shows per-surface progress and capacity forecast
Runbook completed with ownership and rollback thresholds
Canary sequence validated in staging and smoke-tested in two regions
rollout_plan: Preflight week: dry-run of calendar-as-code and notification hooks
Shadow traffic day: runtime + api shadowing for 2 hours in eu-west-1
Canary cohort A: console + api in us-west-2 (2-hour gate)
Canary cohort B: runtime scale test with burst capacity (4-hour gate)
Full ramp: phased regional cutover with capacity hedges and rollback windows
decisions: Use calendar-as-code backed by GitHub actions to enforce release windows (trade-off: added infra but improves repeatability)
Prioritize capacity hedges over batch size increases to avoid tail-latency regressions
Expose a single composite burnup metric for cross-team readout (reduces ambiguity but hides per-service nuance)
blockers: ENG-4782: autoscaler stabilization PR pending (block for runtime ramp)
Security sign-off on console telemetry export (awaiting compliance review)
